messages.author: 4d17bc398c8d91b8
messages.subject: Initialization problems (possibly due to indexing?)
parts:
Hi dear Stan Developers and users,

Thank you for writing such an excellent software! Apart from being fast, it's usually a pleasure to debug (not a statement I tend to write often) 
I am currently trying to implement a hierarchical model to estimate parameters for test kinetics from repeated measurement data. I've managed to write it up so that it compiles, and managed to get a previous
version running and more-or-less converging. Because of missing some observations, I've now had to change from using a wide format, with one column per observation, to a long format, with one row per observation,and therefore had to include an indexing vector to keep track of which individual a particular observation is from.
When trying to run this model, I'm getting the error 

"Error : Rejecting user-specified initialization because of vanishing density.
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done"

From looking over the mailing list archives, this problem seems similar to that reported by Fil Krynecki https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/Rejecting$20user-specified$20initialization/stan-users/QnxFhV9RViE/8APcQn51HBQJ , but there's no solution in that thread.

 I've attached the moderately complex model file. The error is the same whether using init="random", init="0", or using the following initial conditions:

my.inits<-list(
  theta2IgLogmu=log(matrix(rep(c(Xstar=0.15,D=100,a=0.01,S=0.05),each=3),nrow=3)),
  theta1IgLogmu=log(aperm(array(rep(matrix(rep(c(Xstar=0.15,D=100,a=0.01,S=0.05),each=3),nrow=3),
                       N),dim=c(3,4,N)),c(3,1,2))),
  igCorr=aperm(array(rep(diag(4)+(1-diag(4))*0.0001,3),dim=c(4,4,3)),c(3,2,1)),
  igTau=array(rep(rep(1,4),3),dim=c(3,4)),
  omegaCorr=diag(3)+(1-diag(3))*0.0001,
  tau=rep(1,3)*1.5
  )

These conditions seems reasonably close to the real values when comparing to the data.
Any insight and/or suggestion in further bug tracking would be much appreciated!

Best regards,
Gustaf Rydevik

messages.author: 4d17bc398c8d91b8
messages.subject: Re: Initialization problems (possibly due to indexing?)
parts:
And a follow-up: 
As I was generating some example data to go with this post, I discovered that I had a data point of zero, which generated the error. 
Removing the data point solved the problem! My apologies for taking up unnecessary space. 
As a comment/suggestion: Is it possible to have boundaries as <lower>0> (or something similar),
as opposed to <lower=0>? That would have caught this error a bit earlier, and it seems like boundary values are in general discouraged anyway. 

Best regards,
Gustaf

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Initialization problems (possibly due to indexing?)
parts:
We're trying to make debugging even better. I'm going to
take a pass at the parser error messages to try to clean
them up so they're more in user-facing notation and provide
a bit more information when the parser doesn't see the symbol
it's expecting to see.

For constrained continuous values, the bounds are usually
exclusive in practice because of the transforms involved.
We need to make that clearer in the manual for the transforms
and the distributions.

Basically, any time a boundary value for a transform produces an
infinite value, things will break. This is actually what we
want with

real<lower=0> sigma;

because we can't make sense of

y ~ normal(mu,0);

(Yes, we could treat it as a discrete distribution with all its mass
on mu, but that won't work in either HMC or L-BFGS.)

- Bob
